stem: Which feature is found **only** in mammals?

options.content: A backbone made of bony vertebrae
options.rationale: All vertebrates have a backbone.
Only mammals feed their young on milk.
Birds, reptiles and amphibians also have lungs.
Almost all animal groups have eyes.

explanation: Mammary glands (and hair) are found only in mammals. A backbone is shared by all vertebrates, and lungs by birds, reptiles and most amphibians too.

stem: How many legs does an adult insect have?

options.rationale: No arthropod group is defined by four legs.
Insects have three pairs of jointed legs, attached to the thorax.
Eight legs (four pairs) is a feature of arachnids.
That describes myriapods.

explanation: Insects have three pairs of jointed legs (six legs), all attached to the thorax. Arachnids have four pairs, and myriapods have many.

stem: A scorpion has a body in two parts, four pairs of legs and no antennae. Which group of arthropods does it belong to?

options.rationale: Insects have three body parts, three pairs of legs and antennae.
Crustaceans have two pairs of antennae.
Two body parts, four pairs of legs and no antennae are the features of arachnids.
Myriapods have many segments with legs and one pair of antennae.

explanation: Arachnids (spiders, scorpions, ticks) have two body parts, four pairs of legs and no antennae. The scorpion's large pincers are not counted as legs.

stem: The Nile crocodile spends much of its life in water. It has dry skin covered with scales and lays its eggs in a nest on land. Which vertebrate group does it belong to?

options.rationale: Fish have wet scales, fins and gills.
Amphibians have moist skin without scales and lay eggs in water.
Mammals have hair and mammary glands.
Dry, scaly skin and eggs laid on land are reptile features.

explanation: Animals are classified by body features, not habitat. The crocodile's dry, scaly skin and the eggs it lays on land show that it is a reptile.

stem: Which feature shows that the African fish eagle is a bird and **not** a mammal?

options.rationale: Feathers are found only in birds.
Bats are mammals that fly.
Mammals have a backbone too.
Mammals also have lungs.

explanation: Feathers are found only in birds (as are beaks without teeth and hard-shelled eggs). Flight, a backbone and lungs are shared with some or all mammals.

stem: Match each vertebrate group with its main features.

right.content: Hair, mammary glands and external ears
Feathers, a beak and hard-shelled eggs
Dry scales and tough-shelled eggs laid on land
Moist skin without scales and eggs laid in water
A hard exoskeleton and jointed legs

explanation: Each vertebrate group has its own diagnostic features. An exoskeleton with jointed legs describes arthropods, which are not vertebrates.

stem: Match each arthropod group with its features.

right.content: Three body parts, three pairs of legs, one pair of antennae
Two body parts, four pairs of legs, no antennae
Two pairs of antennae, more than four pairs of legs
Many segments with legs, one pair of antennae
Two body parts, three pairs of legs, two pairs of antennae

explanation: Counting body parts, pairs of legs and pairs of antennae separates the four groups. The unused combination does not describe any of them.
hints: Count antennae: insects one pair, arachnids none, crustaceans two pairs, myriapods one pair.

stem: True or false: a spider is an insect.

answerSpec.feedbackTrue: Not true. A spider has eight legs, two body parts and no antennae: it is an arachnid.
answerSpec.feedbackFalse: Correct. Spiders are arachnids, with eight legs and no antennae.

explanation: Spiders have two body parts, four pairs of legs and no antennae, so they are arachnids. Insects have three body parts, three pairs of legs and one pair of antennae.

stem: True or false: bats are birds because they can fly.

answerSpec.feedbackTrue: Not true. Bats have fur and feed their young on milk, so they are mammals.
answerSpec.feedbackFalse: Correct. Bats are mammals: they have fur, external ears and mammary glands.

explanation: Animals are classified by body features, not by how they move. Bats have hair, external ears and mammary glands and no feathers, so they are mammals.

stem: A freshwater crab from the Save River has two pairs of antennae and five pairs of jointed legs. Name the arthropod group it belongs to.

rejected.feedback: Arachnids have no antennae and four pairs of legs.
Insects have three pairs of legs and one pair of antennae.

explanation: Two pairs of antennae and more than four pairs of jointed legs are the features of crustaceans, the group that includes crabs, crayfish and shrimps.

stem: A giant centipede has 21 body segments that carry legs. Each of these segments has one pair of legs. How many legs does it have altogether?
explanation: 21 segments × 1 pair (2 legs) per segment = 42 legs. Centipedes are myriapods: a long body of many segments, most with legs, and one pair of antennae.
workedSolution:
1. Each segment has one pair of legs, which is 2 legs.
2. Total $= 21 \times 2 = 42$ legs.

stem: A tsetse fly has only one pair of wings. Which features show that it is still an insect?

options.content: Its single pair of wings on the thorax
options.rationale: Wings vary among insects; many have two pairs and some have none.

options.content: Three body parts and three pairs of legs
options.rationale: These are the defining features of insects.

options.content: Its hard exoskeleton and jointed legs
options.rationale: All arthropods have an exoskeleton.
Crustaceans also have compound eyes.

explanation: The number of wings varies between insects (flies have one pair, worker termites none). Three body parts (head, thorax, abdomen), three pairs of legs and one pair of antennae are the reliable features of insects.
hints: Which features do all insects share, whether they have wings or not?

stem: The ground pangolin is covered with large, hard scales. It has a few hairs on its face and belly, and the female feeds her young on milk. Which group does it belong to?

options.rationale: Scales alone do not decide the group; mammary glands are found only in mammals.
Fish have wet scales, fins and gills.

options.content: Mammals, because it has hair and feeds its young on milk
options.rationale: Hair and mammary glands are found only in mammals.

options.content: Arthropods, because it has a hard, scaly outer body covering
options.rationale: Its scales grow from its skin; it has a backbone.

explanation: Hair and mammary glands are features found only in mammals, so the pangolin is a mammal even though it has scales. Always look for the feature unique to one group.
hints: Which feature in the description is found in only one vertebrate group?

stem: Complete the sentences comparing frogs and lizards.

payload.template: A frog has {{blank:fskin}} skin and lays eggs {{blank:feggs}}. A lizard has {{blank:lskin}} skin and lays eggs {{blank:leggs}}.

explanation: Frogs are amphibians: moist skin without scales and shell-less eggs laid in water. Lizards are reptiles: dry, scaly skin and eggs with tough shells laid on land.
hints: Frogs are amphibians and lizards are reptiles.

stem:
A class described five animals, A to E.

| Animal | Description |
| --- | --- |
| A | Body in three parts; three pairs of jointed legs; one pair of antennae; two pairs of wings |
| B | Long body of many segments, most with two pairs of legs; one pair of antennae |
| C | Two pairs of antennae; five pairs of jointed legs; breathes with gills |
| D | Moist skin with no scales; lays eggs in water |
| E | Wet scales; fins; breathes with gills |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Match each animal with its group.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Give **two** features of animal C that show it is not an insect.

points.description: It has two pairs of antennae (insects have one pair)
It has five pairs of legs / more than three pairs of legs (insects have three pairs)

parts.explanation: Animal C has two pairs of antennae, but insects have only one pair, and it has five pairs of legs, but insects have three pairs. (Breathing with gills is also typical of crustaceans.)

explanation: A: insect (three body parts, three pairs of legs). B: myriapod (many segments with legs). C: crustacean (two pairs of antennae, more than four pairs of legs). D: amphibian (moist skin, eggs in water). E: fish (wet scales, fins, gills).
hints: For the arthropods, count the antennae and the legs.
Gills are found in both fish and crustaceans: use the other features too.

stem: Describe **two** differences between reptiles and amphibians, and suggest why reptiles are better able than amphibians to live in dry places such as the Zambezi Valley. [4]

points.description: Skin: reptiles have dry skin with scales; amphibians have moist skin without scales
Eggs: reptiles lay eggs with (tough / leathery) shells on land; amphibians lay eggs without shells in water
Dry, scaly skin reduces water loss, so reptiles do not dry out
Shelled eggs do not dry out on land, so reptiles do not need water to breed

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
Reptiles have dry skin covered with scales, while amphibians have moist skin with no scales. Reptiles lay eggs with tough shells on land, but amphibians lay eggs without shells in water, and their tadpoles live in water.

Reptiles cope better in dry places because their scaly skin cuts down water loss, so they do not dry out, and their shelled eggs can survive on land, so they do not need pools of water to breed.

explanation: The features that separate reptiles from amphibians, scaly skin and shelled eggs, are also the features that reduce water loss, allowing reptiles to live and breed away from water.
hints: Think about the skin and the eggs of each group.
Which group would lose water fastest in hot, dry air?

stem: Which feature would show that an unknown arthropod is an arachnid and **not** an insect?

options.rationale: All arthropods have jointed legs.
All arthropods have an exoskeleton.
All arthropods have segmented bodies.

options.content: It has four pairs of legs.
options.rationale: Arachnids have four pairs of legs; insects have three pairs.

explanation: Jointed legs, an exoskeleton and a segmented body are shared by all arthropods. Four pairs of legs (and no antennae) distinguish arachnids from insects.
hints: Which features do all arthropods share, and which differ between the groups?

stem: A chongololo (giant millipede) is a myriapod. Which description fits it?

options.content: Three body parts, three pairs of jointed legs and one pair of antennae
options.rationale: That describes an insect.

options.content: Two body parts, four pairs of legs and no antennae
options.rationale: That describes an arachnid.

options.content: A long body of many segments, most with legs, and one pair of antennae
options.rationale: These are the features of myriapods.

options.content: Two pairs of antennae and five pairs of legs
options.rationale: That describes a crustacean.

explanation: Myriapods (millipedes and centipedes) have a long body made of many similar segments, most carrying legs, and one pair of antennae. Millipedes have two pairs of legs on most segments.

stem: A student classified four animals. Which one has been classified **incorrectly**?

options.rationale: Incorrect: terrapins live partly in water, but they have dry, scaly skin and lay eggs with shells on land, so they are reptiles.
Correct: moist skin without scales, eggs laid in water.
Correct: two pairs of antennae and more than four pairs of legs.
Correct: dry, scaly skin and eggs laid on land.

explanation: The marsh terrapin is the error. Living partly in water and partly on land does not make an animal an amphibian: the terrapin's dry, scaly skin and the shelled eggs it lays on land make it a reptile.
hints: Check each animal against the features of its group, not against where it lives.

stem: Which vertebrate group has moist skin without scales and lays its eggs in water?

options.rationale: Moist, scale-free skin and eggs laid in water are amphibian features.
Fish lay eggs in water but are covered with wet scales.
Reptiles have dry scales and lay eggs on land.
Birds have feathers and lay hard-shelled eggs on land.

explanation: Amphibians, such as frogs and toads, have moist skin without scales and lay shell-less eggs in water; their tadpoles live in water.

stem: True or false: all adult insects have two pairs of wings.

answerSpec.feedbackTrue: Not true. Flies such as the tsetse fly have one pair, and worker termites have none.
answerSpec.feedbackFalse: Correct. Many insects have two pairs of wings, but flies have one pair and some insects have none.

explanation: Wing number varies among insects: flies (including tsetse flies and mosquitoes) have one pair and some insects, such as worker termites, have none. Body parts, legs and antennae are better guides.
hints: Think of a tsetse fly and a worker termite.

stem: Ticks feed on the blood of cattle. An adult tick has a hard exoskeleton, four pairs of jointed legs and no antennae. Its eggs hatch into tiny young ticks with only **three** pairs of legs; they gain a fourth pair when they moult. A student says: "The young ticks are insects, and only the adults are arachnids." Which conclusion is correct?

options.content: The student is right, because the young ticks have three pairs of jointed legs, just like insects.
options.rationale: Young and adults are the same species; one species cannot belong to two groups.

options.content: Ticks are crustaceans, because their number of legs changes as they grow.
options.rationale: Crustaceans have two pairs of antennae; ticks have none.

options.content: Ticks cannot be classified, because their features change.
options.rationale: Many animals change as they develop; species are classified by their adult features.

options.content: The student is wrong: young ticks are the same arachnid species, classified by adult features.
options.rationale: Ticks are arachnids at every stage; the adult has four pairs of legs and no antennae.

explanation: An organism belongs to one species throughout its life, and species are classified by the features of the adult. Adult ticks have four pairs of legs and no antennae, so ticks are arachnids. The six-legged young also have no antennae, unlike insects, which always have one pair.
hints: Can one species belong to two different groups?
Do the young ticks have antennae?
